item.title: Data centres on the ballot: could the AI infrastructure shape US midterms?
item.description: Voters from Ohio to Illinois decide dozens of local measures on Tuesday, as opposition to the giant buildings powering AI cuts across party lines.

item.title: Oleshky residents return to Ukraine
item.description: Residents evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-held territory following a rare local truce. They described years of isolation, food shortages and regular shelling, with some saying they were forced to eat grass and dogs to survive. Seized by Russian forces in the early days of the 2022 invasion, the city remains cut off by the Dnipro River on one side and Russian troops on the other.

item.title: 1 dead, 8 injured in Alabama shooting after football game, police say
item.description: One of the injured was in critical condition, Birmingham police said.

item.title: French high school blockades to restart on Monday, student unions say
item.description: The head of a student union said Sunday that high school blockades throughout France would restart on Monday. French President Emmanuel Macron has called for classes to resume after the government announced new measures to address the ongoing education crisis which student groups found insufficient.

item.title: US Midterms: Democrats face leftward surge
item.description: As Democrats seek to regain control of Congress, divisions within the party are emerging over its future direction. A new wave of progressive candidates is pushing to shift priorities further to the left, challenging corporate money in politics and calling for universal healthcare, climate action and an end to police violence. Monte Francis reports.

item.title: Poland rocked by Constitutional showdown
item.description: Poland’s constitutional crisis deepened on Saturday as the European Commission urged President Karol Nawrocki to recognise new judges appointed by Prime Minister Donald Tusk. The standoff comes ahead of next year’s parliamentary election, with polls suggesting a close race between Tusk’s coalition and the nationalist right. Camille Corcoran reports.

item.title: France: Route du Rhum fleet ready to depart
item.description: The Route du Rhum, billed as the world’s biggest solo transatlantic race, is set to depart from Saint-Malo in Brittany. Skippers will sail alone to Guadeloupe, with professionals and amateur sailors competing in the race, held every four years. Selina Sykes reports.

item.title: Five teenage boys seriously injured after being stabbed at party on Halloween
item.description: Five teenagers have been seriously injured after they were stabbed at a party on Halloween - as police ask for information about an "unknown group".

item.title: Living with high prices in Virginia's 1st Congressional District
item.description: High prices are straining budgets for both a small business owner and a single mom in a rural part of Va.'s 1st Congressional district. They explain how they're handling the economic stress of these times.

item.title: Suspected far-right activists from Britain 'with tear gas bombs' detained in France
item.description: Five suspected far-right activists from Britain were detained in northern France last Thursday, according to authorities.

item.title: It's ACA open enrollment time. Here are the changes for health insurance shoppers
item.description: The ACA health insurance marketplaces — find yours at HealthCare.gov — open Nov. 1 for 2027 coverage. Getting an early start may be especially important this year.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump feeling 'very good' ahead of midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit Iowa and Kansas on Sunday.

item.title: The week in pictures: Lula's victory, Israeli elections and Spain train crash
item.description: From Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's reelection in Brazil's presidential polls, to razor-sharp margins in the Israeli general elections, to a deadly high-speed train collision in Spain, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the most striking images from the past week.

item.title: A day of celebration in Senegal as the Youth Olympic Games get underway
item.description: It is a historic day for Africa and Senegal. For the first time ever, an Olympic competition is being held on African soil. The Youth Olympic Games officially got underway in Senegal in the Dakar region on Saturday, with an opening ceremony attended by 30,000 people. The competition, which brings together 2,700 athletes aged between 14 and 17, will take place across three Senegalese cities, with 25 sports on the programme.

item.title: Senegal hosts first Olympic event on African continent
item.description: Youth Olympics make history with first African Games in over 130 years, opened by Senegal’s president in Dakar. 136 Senegalese athletes are competing, supported by 6,000 local volunteers.

item.title: Youth Olympic Games kick off in Dakar
item.description: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games have officially kicked off in Senegal. Crowds gathered for Saturday's opening ceremony, featuring hundreds of drummers and dancers celebrating Senegalese and wider African culture, in keeping with the Games' motto: “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”. It is the first-ever Olympic sporting event to be held on the African continent, but comes as Senegal faces an economic crisis. The country's president has said he wants to turn sport into an “economic and social engine”. The Games also come amid a government crackdown on LGBTQ+ people. Nearly 3,000 teenagers from more than 200 countries are competing in around a dozen sports, including athletics, beach wrestling and a five-a-side version of baseball. Jean-Loup Chappelet, Professor at Lausanne University and Olympics specialist, shares further insights.

item.title: The World celebrates Halloween: Traditions, costumes and pumpkins
item.description: Halloween celebrations have been embraced in many countries around the world. Charlotte Hughes brings us this round-up.

item.title: France: 115 yachts will sail out of Sain-Malo for Route du Rhum race
item.description: In Saint-Malo, in France's Brittany region, the legendary Route du Rhum is preparing to set sail. Billed as the world's biggest solo transatlantic race, it sees skippers sail alone from France's northern coast to the Caribbean island of Guadeloupe. It's a high-speed, high-risk crossing that takes place every four years.

item.title: US Midterms: Affordability at heart of Michigan race
item.description: For many voters, the cost of living is the single biggest issue. Our reporters Jessica Le Masurier and Sarah Andersen travelled to Michigan to meet voters, where, according to one NGO, around 40% of the population struggle to afford basic necessities.

item.title: Youth-led rallies sweep Europe
item.description: Protests in France have helped inspire youth demonstrations elsewhere in Europe, from Portugal and Italy to Germany. Germany saw particularly large rallies on Saturday, led by a youth initiative whose name roughly translates as “Gen Z has got this”. Demonstrators called for better education and healthcare, stronger climate protection and a more affordable cost of living, while also opposing any return to compulsory military service. However, protests in several major German cities turned violent towards the end of the day, particularly in the financial hub of Frankfurt. Charlotte Hughes reports on the demonstrations across Europe.

item.title: How social media are central to protests
item.description: As we saw in that report, protesters were frustrated at being kept on the outskirts of the French capital. There are also reports of social media posts about the demonstrations being suppressed. Daniel Quinlan has more.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands protest in France for "Act III"
item.description: A heavy police presence was hard to miss on the streets of Paris on Saturday, as the capital saw demonstrations for a third consecutive weekend over the rising cost of living and deteriorating conditions in schools. But the increased security failed to prevent clashes in several parts of the city. Riot police fired tear gas to push back protesters, while small fires broke out in several areas. Similar scenes unfolded across the country, including in Bordeaux, Toulouse and Marseille. Still, the demonstrations were largely less violent than the chaos witnessed on October 17. Caroline Baum has this round-up of the day's events.

item.title: Supreme Court hears religious freedom case centered on universal pre-K program
item.description: The Archdiocese of Denver wants to be able to turn away LGBTQ families from Catholic preschools that receive state funding.

item.title: Here's how to watch election night as the polls close, hour-by-hour
item.description: As polls close on election night, here's a look at what to expect each hour and which midterm races are key to deciding control of Congress.

item.title: What's it like to run for Congress when the odds are stacked heavily against you?
item.description: The majority of congressional races this cycle are rated either solid Democrat or solid Republican. They're the opposite of tossups, where candidates from the minority party face near impossible odds.

item.title: How one family gave a critical boost to gene therapy research
item.description: A family affected by Sanfilippo syndrome raised millions of dollars for research. The Food and Drug Administration just approved a gene therapy the support helped make possible.

item.title: 'Grasping at straws': Judge dismisses Trump suit against Wall Street Journal over Epstein letter
item.description: Saying the president was "grasping at straws," a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Trump claims 'voter fraud' in election race where two candidates share same name
item.description: Federal authorities are carrying out a criminal investigation into a candidate in this Tuesday's US senate election who shares his name with the Republican incumbent amid claims by Donald Trump of "voter fraud".

item.title: National Grid sparks deal to pave way for giant UK data centre
item.description: National Grid has struck a deal paving the way for Britain’s biggest electricity substation to be built on Teesside as the government races to avoid missing out on global demand for AI infrastructure development.

item.title: Binance resumes crypto withdrawals after major hack blamed on North Korea
item.description: Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, on Sunday said it would resume withdrawals after a suspension due to a major hack, which the FBI has tied ​to North Korea. The exchange said it covered 95% of the $6.3 billion in tokens stolen from its platform in the world's largest digital heist.

item.title: Indian opposition parties stage mega rally seeking election chief’s resignation
item.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators on Sunday joined a protest in New Delhi called by Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and backed by the youth “Cockroach” movement amid tight security. Protesters are demanding the resignation of the country's election chief over voter list revisions that critics say favour Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

item.title: Bulgarians vote in presidential runoff amid security tensions in the Black Sea
item.description: Bulgarians voted Sunday in a presidential runoff between two candidates with opposing views on the Ukraine war and relations with Russia as tensions mount in the Black Sea. Incumbent President Iliana Iotova, who favours dialogue with Moscow, faces off against Andrey Gyurov, a former caretaker prime minister backed by the pro-Western opposition.

item.description: While the spotlight will be on the nearly 60,000 people running the course, they would not be there without the help of thousands of volunteers on the sidelines.

item.description: The King will speak about slavery with "unflinching honesty" and "sincere sorrow" in a speech to Commonwealth leaders amid increasing pressure for Britain to offer an apology over its role in the transatlantic slave trade.

item.title: UN demands investigation into death of staff member in Houthi custody
item.description: A Yemeni staff member of the UN Human Rights Office has died in Houthi custody after being arbitrarily held for more ​than two years, the UN human rights chief has said.

Tensions flared ​at the end of marches in ​some cities but authorities reported that most demonstrations were largely peaceful.

Organized by the "GenZ regelt!" ("Gen Z has got this!") group, marches were held nationwide to demand more funding for education and to protest the high cost of living.
